red: Day: ABI C02 (0.64) red + synthetic green; Night: IR C13
note: Day true-color-like; night IR clouds white, low cloud/fog light blue, static VIIRS city-lights background. Uses ~5 ABI channels.
global_port: Recipe is CIRA-proprietary; TAT's own GeoColor-style path already exists. AHI/AMI/FCI have needed bands.
source: NOAA NESDIS / GOES-R quick guide (verified: 'GeoColor uses five ABI channels, day vs night')

green: Synthetic green (0.45*C02 + 0.10*C03 + 0.45*C01, CIMSS recipe) - ABI lacks native green
note: Daylight only. Himawari/AHI & MTG/FCI have a NATIVE green (0.51) band -> cleaner true color without synthesis.
global_port: Portable; better on AHI/AGRI/AMI/FCI (native green). Sunlight-only.
source: CIMSS/CIRA synthetic-green (Bah et al.); widely documented

note: Semi-transparent color-enhanced IR C13 (BT) overlaid on high-res VIS C02 - reveals cloud-top texture + temperature together. Alpha blend, not additive RGB.
global_port: Fully portable (needs one VIS + one clean IR). Excellent for convection/OT.

note: Highlights jet/dynamic tropopause, PV, dry intrusions, warm/cold air masses. Limited at high viewing angle (limb).
global_port: Portable to SEVIRI/AHI/FCI with matching WV+O3 bands. AHI ozone approximate.
source: EUMETSAT/NOAA Air Mass quick guide (verified; limb limitation noted)

note: SEVIRI heritage R=IR12.0-IR10.8, G=IR10.8-IR8.7, B=IR10.8. Dust = magenta/pink. 24h.
global_port: Highly portable (window channels on all modern imagers).
source: EUMeTrain/EUMETSAT Dust RGB quick guide (verified band diffs)

note: Hot fire pixels bright red/orange/yellow by temperature. Often overlaid semi-transparent on GeoColor.
global_port: Portable where SWIR/MWIR bands exist (AHI/AMI/FCI yes).
source: NOAA/CIRA Fire Temperature quick guide (verified; Camp Fire example NESDIS)

note: Separates ice vs water clouds + snow; daytime. Good for convective initiation.
source: NOAA/CIRA Day Cloud Phase quick guide

note: Fog/low-cloud detection at night; fog appears distinct color. 24h-capable variant of day microphysics.
source: EUMETSAT Night Microphysics quick guide (verified; IR3.9-IR10.8 BTD for fog)

note: Severe/updraft signatures; overshooting tops, strong updrafts stand out.
source: EUMETSAT Day Convection RGB quick guide
